name: Crucible Industries Boarding SMG BSM-6 'Cutlass'
description:
The BSM-6 Cutlass is purpose-built for maritime and orbital boarding operations, featuring a waterproof sealed action, a built-in breaching tool at the muzzle, and an integrated magnetic clamp on the underside that locks the weapon to ferrous surfaces when the operator needs both hands free. The weapon fires 10mm caseless from a 20-round magazine with a controlled 550 rpm rate designed for deliberate room-clearing rather than suppressive spray.

The Cutlass's breaching tool is a hardened steel prow at the muzzle that functions as a prying bar, glass breaker, and emergency melee weapon. The BCI integration includes a structural analysis overlay that identifies weak points in doors, hatches, and bulkheads for the breaching tool, and a decompression risk calculator for orbital operations that warns operators before firing in areas with hull integrity concerns.

Crucible developed the Cutlass in response to the growing piracy problem on GLMZ's maritime trade routes and the security needs of orbital stations. At Φ3,500, it is priced for organizational procurement by security firms, ship crews, and station operators who need a weapon designed for the unique challenges of forced entry in sealed environments.
specifications: caliber: 10mm caseless effective_range: 50m rate_of_fire: 550 rpm (cyclic) magazine_capacity: 20 rounds weight: 2.5 kg
tactical_use: The Cutlass is a specialist boarding weapon. Its breaching tool eliminates the need for a separate entry tool, its magnetic clamp frees hands for climbing and movement through zero-G environments, and its sealed action functions after full submersion. The 10mm round provides the stopping power needed to end close-quarters engagements quickly in confined spaces where prolonged firefights risk structural damage. The decompression calculator prevents operators from creating lethal hull breaches with their own weapons.
cultural_context: The Cutlass has been adopted by both sides of maritime conflict — security forces and pirates alike carry BSM-6s because the weapon is simply the best tool for the job. Crucible officially condemns piracy while acknowledging that they cannot control secondary market sales. In port communities, the Cutlass is as common as a boat hook, and its distinctive muzzle prow makes it instantly recognizable.
story_hooks: A pirate crew's Cutlass weapons all share sequential serial numbers — they were stolen directly from a Crucible shipment meant for a security firm. The firm is demanding Crucible replace them, and Crucible is demanding the firm explain how an entire shipment was hijacked.

An orbital station boarding team discovered their Cutlass decompression calculators had been miscalibrated. If they had fired in the section they were clearing, they would have breached the hull and killed everyone aboard.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular SMG with a pronounced hardened steel prow extending from the muzzle like a ship's cutlass. The profile is aggressively utilitarian—all sharp edges and functional geometry, with a distinctly maritime aesthetic. The underside features a visible magnetic mounting plate that sits flush with the lower receiver.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 58cm | Barrel length: 20cm | Width at receiver: 8cm | Height with charging handle: 12cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and balanced—2.5 kg feels substantial in hand but purposefully distributed for one-handed operation in confined spaces. The forward weight of the breaching tool is intentional, not awkward.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer frame with stainless steel internal action and hardened tool-steel breaching prow. Waterproof sealed receivers throughout.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with brushed stainless steel accents around the action. The breaching tool is left unpolished tool-steel—functional gray with light oxidation patina. BCI interface port is gunmetal gray.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with stainless steel and tool-steel accents. BCI status indicator strip runs along the upper receiver in deep blue.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured rubberized polymer with tight knurling—designed to maintain grip when wet or in vacuum gloves. The grip is slightly oversized for gloved operation.
distinctive_features: Hardened steel breaching prow at muzzle (functional as pry bar, glass breaker, melee tool)
Flush-mounted magnetic clamp plate on underside (ferrous surface lock mechanism)
BCI integration port on upper rail with recessed connectors
Decompression risk calculator indicator (amber/red warning light above magazine well)
Sealed action shrouds with drain ports
Cross-mounted charging handle designed for vacuum glove operation
Integrated cable management routing along frame
Rail system designed for compact magnetic accessories only (no standard picatinny)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES logo stamped on left side of receiver (bold sans-serif in raised letters). Serial number and waterproofing certification etched on right side. BCI compatibility mark on upper rail. Breach tool rated for tool use: 'PRYING / BREACHING ONLY' stenciled in white on steel prow.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained, well-cared-for. Salt spray corrosion resistant coating shows minor wear on high-contact areas (grip, breaching tool tip). Magnetic clamp shows faint ferrous dust residue. BCI indicator lens typically shows minimal scratching from repeated use.
